title: A platelet size–count interaction fails to improve cross-cycle prediction of elevated CRP beyond standard blood-count and adiposity measures
abstract: A discovery-centered log platelet-count by log mean-platelet-volume interaction was fitted in 5,430 NHANES 2009–2010 adults and tested in 4,814 separately recruited 2015–2016 adults. For single-visit CRP >3 mg/L, adding the interaction to demographic, adiposity and blood-count predictors changed survey-weighted Brier score by +0.000533 (95% fixed-model stratified PSU-bootstrap interval −0.000089 to +0.001122; delete-PSU jackknife interval −0.000342 to +0.001408). The predicted improvement was not established. Smoking adjustment and exclusion of CRP >10 mg/L did not reverse the unfavorable point estimate, while a post-primary raw platelet/MPV comparator yielded a near-zero favorable change. This is a negative test of a specific predictive representation, not evidence that platelet biology contains no inflammatory information. Assay differences, complete-case selection and shared survey infrastructure limit interpretation. Public inputs, hashes, code and author self-checks accompany the report.
